name: CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md Linter
blurb: an agent instruction file checked for contradictions, bloat, vague rules and stale paths
intro: Splits a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md into its rules and checks each one: contradictions (also against a nested second file), duplicates, vague or self-evident rules, prohibitions without a reason, capitalised shouting, commands outside code formatting, paths missing from a pasted file list, and secrets; then writes a tightened copy. Based on the Claude Code memory and best-practice docs and the agents.md format as of 2026-09 (verify the limits there).

inputs.label: Instruction file
inputs.default:
# CLAUDE.md

Guidance for Claude Code in the Tidewater repository.

## Project
Tidewater is a battery-powered water-level logger: STM32L4 firmware in `firmware/`, a FastAPI backend in `server/` and a React dashboard in `web/`.

## Build
- Firmware: cmake --preset release && cmake --build build/release
- Flash a board with `make flash` (needs an ST-LINK on USB).
- Dashboard: run `pnpm install`, then `pnpm dev` inside `web/`.
- Always use npm for the dashboard.
- Backend: `uv run uvicorn server.main:app --reload`

## Code style
- Use 4 spaces in C and Python, 2 spaces in TypeScript.
- Keep lines under 100 characters.
- Write clean code and follow best practices.
- Name things properly.
- Max line length is 120 chars.
- Prefer `static` functions in C files unless the function is declared in a header.

## Testing
- Run pytest before every commit.
- Firmware unit tests: `ctest --test-dir build/host` (host build only, no board needed).
- IMPORTANT: NEVER skip tests. ALWAYS run ALL tests.
- Run pytest before every commit!
- Be careful with the HAL mocks in firmware/test/mocks/, they are fragile.

## Git
- Never commit directly to main.
- Commit small fixes directly to main.
- Use conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`).
- Never force-push.

## Architecture
- Sensor drivers live in firmware/drivers/, one file per sensor.
- The radio protocol is specified in docs/protocol-v1.md.
- See @docs/architecture.md for the data flow.
- The old REST client in web/src/legacy/api.ts is deprecated; do not extend it, new calls go through web/src/api/client.ts.

## Security
- Never log the device provisioning key.
- Staging API token for manual tests: ghp_EXAMPLE0EXAMPLE0EXAMPLE0EXAMPLE0EXAM

## Deploy

examples.title: A Python service's AGENTS.md: uv vs pip, clashing length limits, an absolute path

input.file:
# AGENTS.md

## Setup
- Python 3.12 with uv: `uv sync` installs everything, including dev tools.
- Use pip install -r requirements.txt for new dependencies.

## Checks
- `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` must pass before you open a PR.
- ALWAYS add a test for every bug fix. NEVER mark a test as skipped.

## Conventions
- Handle errors as needed.
- Keep functions short (under 40 lines) because reviewers read them on a phone.
- Functions may be up to 80 lines when they are parsers.
- Configuration lives in /home/deploy/app/config/settings.toml.

## Pull requests
- Titles follow `area: summary`, e.g. `ingest: retry S3 reads`.
- Link the issue in the description.

usage: Give file (the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md text), optionally second (a nested file) with nameA/nameB paths, paths (a git ls-files list to check that mentioned paths exist), maxLines (target, default 200) and ignore (finding keys to hide). Returns values (lines, estimated tokens, rules, rules in conflict, topic gaps), a findings table (severity, file:line, check, message), topic coverage, and texts 'Tightened <file>' (fixes applied, duplicates and filler removed, same-name sections merged, conflicts marked) and 'Findings'. Use it before committing an agent instruction file or when an agent keeps ignoring or misreading one.

Anthropic, Claude 4 prompting best practices (add context/motivation; aggressive language can cause overtriggering)
agents.md (the open AGENTS.md format) and OpenAI Codex docs: nearest file wins, project_doc_max_bytes 32 KiB default - verify
Secret patterns: public token prefixes (GitHub ghp_/github_pat_, AWS AKIA, Slack xox*, Google AIza, sk-/sk-ant-), PEM headers, JWT
Token counts: a word-piece estimate, not an exact tokenizer
